assignments.title: Recitation: A Passage from the Forest
assignments.html:
Recitation: A Passage from the Forest
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Recitation
3 points (completion)About 1 minuteRecord / Upload MediaDue in Week 3
The recitation
 
Record a reading of one of the three passages below, about one minute long. Prose has no meter; the performance lives in pacing, emphasis, and tone. Reading from the page is permitted.
What to do
 
1Choose one passage. Option A, B, or C below. All three are public domain.
2Mark and rehearse. Read it aloud three times. Mark the words that carry weight and the pauses.
3Record and submit. One take, about a minute. Say your name and your option first.
Choose one passage
 
Option A: the lingering in the forest, Chapter XVII (148 words). Narration: a held moment.
Option B: Hester’s argument for leaving, Chapter XVII (122 words). Speech: persuasion.
Option C: the sunshine, Chapter XVIII (146 words). Narration: release.
OPTION A · THE SCARLET LETTER, CHAPTER XVII (HAWTHORNE, 1850)

The forest was obscure around them, and creaked with a blast that was passing through it. The boughs were tossing heavily above their heads; while one solemn old tree groaned dolefully to another, as if telling the sad story of the pair that sat beneath, or constrained to forebode evil to come.

And yet they lingered. How dreary looked the forest-track that led backward to the settlement, where Hester Prynne must take up again the burden of her ignominy, and the minister the hollow mockery of his good name! So they lingered an instant longer. No golden light had ever been so precious as the gloom of this dark forest. Here, seen only by his eyes, the scarlet letter need not burn into the bosom of the fallen woman! Here, seen only by her eyes, Arthur Dimmesdale, false to God and man, might be, for one moment, true!

OPTION B · THE SCARLET LETTER, CHAPTER XVII, HESTER SPEAKING

Doth the universe lie within the compass of yonder town, which only a little time ago was but a leaf-strewn desert, as lonely as this around us? Whither leads yonder forest-track? Backward to the settlement, thou sayest! Yes; but onward, too. Deeper it goes, and deeper, into the wilderness, less plainly to be seen at every step; until, some few miles hence, the yellow leaves will show no vestige of the white man’s tread. There thou art free! So brief a journey would bring thee from a world where thou hast been most wretched, to one where thou mayest still be happy! Is there not shade enough in all this boundless forest to hide thy heart from the gaze of Roger Chillingworth?

OPTION C · THE SCARLET LETTER, CHAPTER XVIII

Her sex, her youth, and the whole richness of her beauty, came back from what men call the irrevocable past, and clustered themselves, with her maiden hope, and a happiness before unknown, within the magic circle of this hour. And, as if the gloom of the earth and sky had been but the effluence of these two mortal hearts, it vanished with their sorrow. All at once, as with a sudden smile of heaven, forth burst the sunshine, pouring a very flood into the obscure forest, gladdening each green leaf, transmuting the yellow fallen ones to gold, and gleaming adown the gray trunks of the solemn trees. The objects that had made a shadow hitherto, embodied the brightness now. The course of the little brook might be traced by its merry gleam afar into the wood’s heart of mystery, which had become a mystery of joy.

Chapter XVII (Options A and B) ↗Chapter XVIII (Option C) ↗
Record it
 
Use either tool; both earn full credit:
☐the Canvas media recorder built into this assignment, or
☐a phone recording, uploaded to the assignment.
How this is scored
 
Completion rubric, 3 points.
PointEarned when
1The full passage is performed (about one minute), read expressively or from memory.
2The recording is clear and audible, with deliberate pacing and a tone a listener can name.
3The recording is submitted to this assignment on time.
Done when
 
☐I read one full passage, about a minute long
☐You can hear every word, and the pacing and tone were my choice
☐I said my name and my option first
☐My recording is submitted here
Submit
 
Submit the recording through this assignment (record in Canvas or upload the file). An uploaded file is named LastName_FirstName_Recitation6_ELA9.

assignments.html:
The Scarlet Letter Literary Analysis Essay
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter
100 pointsWord essay, 900 to 1,200 wordsProject PDF
Choose one prompt
 
A. The letter. Hawthorne lets the meaning of the scarlet letter change. What changes it: the community or Hester?
B. The minister. Does Dimmesdale’s public confession redeem him, or does it come too late?
C. The theme. What does a community owe the person it judges, and what does a person owe the truth? Argue what the novel answers.
The essay must
 
☐Length: 900 to 1,200 words, not counting the Works Cited page.
☐State one arguable thesis in the introduction.
☐Quote the novel at least three times, each introduced and cited by chapter, like this: (Hawthorne, ch. 6).
☐Use one researched source beyond the novel, woven into your argument, cited in the text, and listed in Works Cited.
☐Include a counterclaim paragraph with a concession and a rebuttal.
☐Use MLA format: Times New Roman 12 point, double-spaced, last name and page number in the header, a heading block, a title, and a Works Cited page.
Upload
 
Upload two files: your Word essay (.docx) and your project PDF.

CriterionStrongDevelopingBeginning

30 points		The thesis is arguable and specific, and every paragraph advances it. The counterclaim is stated fairly and answered with evidence.The thesis is present but general, or some paragraphs drift. The counterclaim is thin or answered without evidence.No clear thesis; the essay summarizes the plot. No counterclaim.
Textual evidence and quotation
25 points		At least three well-chosen quotations, accurate, introduced, cited by chapter, and explained.Quotations are present but dropped in, uncited, or explained only briefly.Fewer than three quotations, or evidence is inaccurate or missing.
Researched source and MLA
25 points		The source is credible, woven into the argument, cited in the text, and correct in Works Cited.The source is present but stacked beside the argument, or citations contain errors.No source, or the source is unused or uncited.
Organization and conventions
20 points		Clear introduction, body, and conclusion; transitions guide the reader; MLA format and length met; nearly error-free.The structure is visible but uneven; some format or length issues; some errors.The structure is unclear; length or format missing; frequent errors.
Done when
 
☐My thesis answers my prompt in an arguable sentence
☐I quoted the novel at least three times, each exact and cited by chapter

Week 1 Quiz
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Week 1
15 points15 questionsOne attempt

questions.text: In Chapter I, the narrator says the founders of a new colony soon set aside ground for two things. What are they?

answers.text: a church and a school
a cemetery and a prison
a courthouse and a market-place
a meeting-house and a common

questions.text: What grows beside the prison door in Chapter I?

answers.text: a wild rose-bush
an apple tree planted by the founders
an old oak that once shaded the scaffold
a vine planted by the jailer

questions.text: In Chapter III, a townsman explains Hester's sentence to the stranger. What is it?

answers.text: three hours on the platform of the pillory, then a mark of shame on her bosom for the rest of her life
a public whipping, then banishment into the forest
a year in prison, then the loss of her child to the town
three hours on the pillory, then a fine paid to the magistrates

questions.text: Standing on the scaffold in Chapter II, Hester sees scenes from her past. Which scene is among them?

answers.text: her native village in Old England and her father's decayed house of gray stone
her wedding in the Boston meeting-house
the voyage across the Atlantic with her husband
her first meeting with the governor

questions.text: Where does Hester live after her release (Ch. V)?

answers.text: in a room above the prison, by order of the magistrates
in a small thatched cottage on the outskirts of the town, apart from other houses
in the governor's household, where she sews for his family
in a village a day's walk from Boston

questions.text: Why does Hester name her daughter Pearl (Ch. VI)?

answers.text: Pearl was her own mother's name.
The child was "of great price," bought with all Hester had.
The minister chose the name at the baptism.
The name hides the child's father's family.

questions.text: Hester braces herself for "the stings and venomous stabs of public contumely" (Ch. II). Contumely means

answers.text: curiosity
insulting scorn
legal punishment
pity

questions.text: The narrator calls Pearl an "emblem and product of sin" (Ch. VI). Here emblem means

answers.text: a punishment handed down by a court
an object or figure that stands for an idea
a secret kept from the town
a mark stitched onto clothing by law

questions.text: Hester lives "of the plainest and most ascetic description" (Ch. V). An ascetic life is one that

answers.text: is spent in hiding from others
denies itself comfort and pleasure
is devoted to study and books
depends on charity from neighbors

questions.text: Which word names an act of suffering or self-denial taken on to make up for a wrong?

answers.text: iniquity
alchemy
penance
pillory

questions.text: The women at the prison door want to handle "such malefactresses as this Hester Prynne" (Ch. II). A malefactress is a woman who

answers.text: has committed a crime
speaks against the magistrates
is new to the colony
refuses to attend church

questions.text: Chillingworth speaks of his "old studies in alchemy" (Ch. IV). Alchemy was

answers.text: the study of the stars to foretell events
an early science that tried to turn common metals into gold
the practice of law in the colonies
the art of healing with prayer

questions.text: Which part of this sentence is the participial phrase? Hester, gathering the infant to her bosom, stepped out into the sunshine.

answers.text: Hester stepped out
gathering the infant to her bosom
into the sunshine
out into the sunshine

questions.text: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?

answers.text: Clutching the infant, Hester faced the crowd.
Clutching the infant, the crowd watched Hester.
Hester, clutching the infant, faced the crowd.
Hester faced the crowd, clutching the infant.

questions.text: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

answers.text: The crowd waited in silence; however, Hester would not speak.
The crowd waited in silence, however, Hester would not speak.
The crowd waited in silence; however Hester would not speak.
The crowd waited in silence however; Hester would not speak.

15 points15 questionsOne attempt

questions.text: In Chapter VII, why does Hester go to the Governor’s mansion?

answers.text: To ask that the scarlet letter be taken off her gown.
To bring the gloves and to keep her child.
To ask the Governor’s leave to sail back to England.
To complain to the Governor about the children who threw mud at Pearl.

questions.text: Asked who made her, what does Pearl tell Mr. Wilson (Ch. VIII)?

answers.text: That God made her, as the catechism teaches.
That her mother sewed her together out of scarlet velvet.
That she was plucked off the rose-bush by the prison door.
That she does not know and will not be taught by Mr. Wilson.

questions.text: What does the Governor decide at the end of the hearing (Ch. VIII)?

answers.text: To leave Pearl with her mother, as long as there is no scandal.
To take Pearl at once and give her to Mr. Wilson to raise.
To place Pearl in a godly household and let Hester visit her each month.
To keep the matter open until the elders can meet and vote on it.

questions.text: Why do the physician and the minister come to live in the same house (Ch. IX)?

answers.text: The minister asks the physician to move in so that the two men can study together.
The Governor orders it so that the town can keep watch over the stranger.
The physician buys the house from a widow and invites the minister to live there.
The minister’s friends arrange it so the physician can watch his health.

questions.text: What does the physician do while the minister sleeps in his chair (Ch. X)?

answers.text: He wakes the minister and demands that he confess his secret at once.
He pushes aside the vestment, then turns away in wild wonder.
He mixes a sleeping draught into the minister’s cup of medicine.
He reads the minister’s private papers and puts them back in place.

questions.text: In Chapter XII, the minister cries out from the scaffold at midnight. Where does Hester say she has been?

answers.text: Gathering herbs in the forest at night to sell to the physician in town
Sitting up all night with a sick child in a cottage near the shore
At Governor Winthrop’s death-bed, taking his measure for a robe
Walking along the shore with Pearl, who could not sleep that night

questions.text: In Chapter XII, what does the sexton say the great red letter in the sky stands for?

answers.text: Angel, for Governor Winthrop, who died that night.
Alarm, a warning that war is coming to the colony.
Apostle, for the minister’s sermon the next morning.
Amen, the close of the town’s prayers for the governor.

questions.text: Which word means a sign that something important is about to happen?

answers.text: portent
vigil
caprice
expiation

questions.text: Chillingworth confronts “the emaciated and white-cheeked minister” (Ch. X). Here emaciated means

answers.text: weak from long hours of prayer
angry and quick to quarrel
unwilling to speak openly
extremely thin from illness

questions.text: Made-up example: Long after the quarrel, she still felt such ______ for her harsh words that she could not sleep.

answers.text: caprice
portent
remorse
antipathy

questions.text: The minister draws “the long, deep, and tremulous breath” (Ch. XI) before he speaks. Here tremulous means

answers.text: slow, calm and steady
quivering or shaking
loud and ringing
cold and hard

questions.text: Made-up example: Without a single clue to go on, he knew by ______ that someone was watching him.

answers.text: expiation
sagacity
observation
intuition

questions.text: Made-up example: His lantern swinging at his side, Mr. Wilson walked slowly home. Which part is the absolute phrase?

answers.text: His lantern swinging at his side
Mr. Wilson walked slowly home
swinging at his side, Mr. Wilson walked
his side, Mr. Wilson walked slowly home

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence uses an absolute phrase correctly?

answers.text: Pearl ran from the hall her tunic flashing red in the sun.
Pearl ran from the hall, her tunic flashing red in the sun.
Pearl ran from the hall, her tunic was flashing red in the sun.
Pearl ran from the hall. Her tunic flashing red in the sun.

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence is parallel?

answers.text: The minister fasted, kept vigils, and was studying late into the night.
The minister fasting, kept vigils, and he studied late into the night.
The minister fasted, kept vigils, and studied late into the night.
The minister fasted, vigils were kept, and studied late into the night.

quizzes.title: Week 3 Quiz
quizzes.description:
Week 3 Quiz
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Week 3
15 points15 questionsOne attempt

questions.text: In Chapter XIII, the narrator says that if Pearl had never come to Hester, Hester might have become

answers.text: a teacher of the town’s children and their mothers
the wife of one of the magistrates of the colony
the founder of a new religious group
a healer who traveled from one settlement to the next

questions.text: In Chapter XIV, why does Hester tell Chillingworth she must reveal to the minister who he is?

answers.text: She owes the minister a debt of truth.
The magistrates have ordered her to speak out.
Chillingworth has threatened to harm Pearl if she waits.
She hopes to win back her place in the town by doing it.

questions.text: After Chillingworth goes away, what does Hester say she feels toward him (Ch. XV)?

answers.text: Pity, because so much good has been wasted in his nature
Fear, because he has threatened to harm her child
Gratitude, because of the care he has given the minister
Hatred, though she blames herself for feeling it

questions.text: In Chapter XVI, Pearl asks whether her mother ever met the Black Man, the Devil of Puritan folklore. What does Hester answer?

answers.text: That there is no such being anywhere in the forest at all
That she met him once, and the letter is his mark
That only Mistress Hibbins has ever met him in the forest
That Pearl must never speak of him again to anyone

questions.text: In Chapter XVII, Hester tells the minister that Chillingworth is her husband. How does he first answer her?

answers.text: He thanks her for the warning and asks what he should do.
He forgives her at once, before she has finished asking.
He says he half knew it, and cannot forgive her.
He denies it and says the physician has been a loyal friend.

questions.text: Which of these does Hester do right after she throws the scarlet letter aside (Ch. XVIII)?

answers.text: She takes off her cap and lets her hair fall.
She kneels at the brook and washes her hands clean of it.
She asks the minister to carry the letter back to town.
She calls Pearl to come and hold the letter for her.

questions.text: In Chapter XIX, after the minister kisses Pearl on the brow, what does she do?

answers.text: She takes his hand and walks off with him.
She asks him for his blessing.
She kisses the scarlet letter on her mother’s breast instead.
She runs to the brook and washes the kiss away.

questions.text: Which word means ruling with total power, like a tyrant?

answers.text: benign
despotic
avowed
estranged

questions.text: Made-up example: The old sailor kept a carved stone in his pocket, sure that it would protect him at sea. It was his ______.

answers.text: penitence
speculation
vivacity
talisman

questions.text: Hester has “such latitude of speculation” that the minister finds her thinking foreign (Ch. XVIII). Here speculation means

answers.text: deep thinking about questions with no sure answer
buying and selling goods in the hope of a quick profit
a strict habit of obeying every rule
careful watching of what other people do

questions.text: In “the despondency of a broken spirit” (Ch. XVII), despondency means

answers.text: nervous fear of being found out
low spirits from losing hope
weakness of the body from illness
a stubborn refusal to speak

questions.text: In “what men call the irrevocable past” (Ch. XVIII), irrevocable means

answers.text: openly admitted or declared
full of lively high spirits
impossible to take back or undo
deeply sorry for having done wrong

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence is inverted correctly?

answers.text: Seldom had Pearl stood so still.
Seldom Pearl had stood so still.
Seldom did Pearl stood so still.
Seldom had stood Pearl so still at all.

questions.text: Which of these questions is a rhetorical question, asked to make a point and not to get an answer?

answers.text: “Didst thou ever awake, and find thy mother gone?” (Ch. XVI)
“What evil have I done the man?” (Ch. XIV)
“hast thou found peace?” (Ch. XVII)
“Dost thou think the child will be glad to know me?” (Ch. XVIII)

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence reports Pearl’s question with the right punctuation?

answers.text: Pearl asked, why does the minister keep his hand over his heart.
“Why does the minister keep his hand over his heart.” asked Pearl.
Pearl asked why the minister kept his hand over his heart.
Pearl asked why the minister kept his hand over his heart?

quizzes.title: Week 4 Quiz
quizzes.description:
Week 4 Quiz
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Week 4
15 points15 questionsOne attempt

questions.text: In Chapter XX, why does the minister think it fortunate that the ship leaves when it does?

answers.text: Chillingworth will have left Boston long before it sails.
Hester will have time to sell the last of her needlework.
The deacons will have time to find a new pastor for the church.
He can preach the Election Sermon first.

questions.text: According to the narrator, why does the minister feel wicked impulses on the walk home (Ch. XX)?

answers.text: Mistress Hibbins cast a spell on him in the forest.
He chose what he knew was sin, and it spread.
Chillingworth’s medicine has left him feverish.
The walk has worn him out past all self-control.

questions.text: In Chapter XXI, what reason does Hester give Pearl for the holiday mood in the market-place?

answers.text: A new ruler is beginning to govern.
A ship has come in from England with news for the colony.
The town is welcoming its minister home from a long journey.
The Governor has given the people a free feast for the day.

questions.text: In Chapter XXI, why can Hester and the shipmaster talk without being overheard?

answers.text: The music of the procession is too loud for anyone to hear them.
They meet inside the ship’s cabin down at the wharf.
No one steps into the open space around her.
The beadle keeps the crowd back from the two of them.

questions.text: In Chapter XXII, Pearl asks whether the man in the procession is the same minister who kissed her by the brook. How does Hester answer?

answers.text: She hushes her, since the forest is not talked of here.
She says it was a different minister who only looks like him.
She promises that he will greet them kindly after the sermon.
She says the minister did not see them in the crowd today.

questions.text: In Chapter XXIII, the minister asks whether this is better than what they dreamed of in the forest. How does Hester answer?

answers.text: She says yes, because the whole town will forgive them now.
She says yes, because Pearl will at last be safe from Chillingworth.
She says no, because he should have spoken seven years sooner.
She says she does not know, and speaks of dying.

questions.text: In Chapter XXIV, what does Chillingworth’s will do?

answers.text: It leaves everything to Hester, as his lawful wife.
It gives his books and herbs to the town.
It leaves property here and in England to Pearl.
It gives his whole fortune to the church.

questions.text: Which word means complete honesty and uprightness?

answers.text: obeisance
probity
preternatural
conjectural

questions.text: Made-up example: As the king passed, each courtier made a deep ______.

answers.text: obeisance
consternation
probity
fidelity

questions.text: In “it was the venerable John Wilson” (Ch. XXIII), venerable means

answers.text: old and ready to retire from public life
deserving respect for age and character
dressed in fine, formal clothes
quick to anger and slow to forgive

questions.text: To repudiate a rumor is to

answers.text: prove it with careful evidence
pass it on to everyone you know
guess at where it began
reject it as untrue

questions.text: Made-up example: The old dog’s ______ to his master never wavered, even in the worst winter.

answers.text: consternation
probity
fidelity
obeisance

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence is built on antithesis?

answers.text: The town called him a saint; he called himself a sinner.
The town called him a saint, a scholar, and a leader.
The town called him a saint because he preached so well.
The town called him a saint, and he agreed with them for years.

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence is a chiasmus?

answers.text: Hester left the town, and Pearl left it too.
Hester left the town; the town never left her.
Hester left the town and never looked back.
Hester left the town; years later she came home.

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence about Mistress Hibbins uses precise words the text can prove?

answers.text: Mistress Hibbins was a crazy old witch who loved to blab to anyone.
Mistress Hibbins was a nosy gossip who loved to stir up trouble.
Mistress Hibbins said she knew the minister had visited the forest.
Mistress Hibbins was a wicked old hag who wanted to see him ruined at last.

quizzes.title: Week 5 Quiz
quizzes.description:
Week 5 Quiz
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Week 5
15 points15 questionsOne attempt

questions.text: In Chapter XII, who looks out from a window of the Governor’s house when the minister cries out?

answers.text: The Governor and his sister
Mr. Wilson, from his study at the end of the street
Hester, from her cottage on the edge of the shore
The physician, from a room in the minister’s house

questions.text: In Chapter XII, the minister bursts into laughter on the scaffold. What is he picturing?

answers.text: Chillingworth failing to find him at home
Pearl and Hester climbing up beside him
Mr. Wilson climbing the steps with his lantern
The town finding him there at dawn

questions.text: In Chapter XIII, which group is slower to soften toward Hester?

answers.text: The poor, whom she feeds and nurses in their homes
The children, who once mocked her in the street
The rulers and the learned men
The women who watched her stand on the platform

questions.text: In Chapter XXIII, an older minister steps forward to steady the minister as he walks. What does the minister do?

answers.text: He leans on the old man’s arm and thanks him warmly.
He pushes the old man’s arm away.
He asks the old man to walk ahead of him instead.
He stops and waits until the old man goes away.

questions.text: In Chapter XXIV, what do some of the spectators deny?

answers.text: That the minister preached the sermon that day at all
That Hester stood on the platform beside the minister
That the physician was in the crowd at the end of it
That a mark was there on his breast

questions.text: In Chapter XXIV, why does Hester come back to New England?

answers.text: It is her own choice: her penitence is here.
The magistrates order her to return to the town and wear it.
Pearl sends for her from across the sea.
She has heard that her old cottage is about to be sold.

questions.text: In Chapter XXIII, how does the crowd explain the sad undertone of the sermon?

answers.text: They suspect a secret sin in his past.
They think he is leaving for England.
They think he will soon die.
They fear the colony faces ruin.

questions.text: Which word means deep public disgrace, a bad name known to all?

answers.text: efficacy
infamy
pathos
eminence

questions.text: The night sky is covered “from zenith to horizon” (Ch. XII). Here zenith means

answers.text: the point straight overhead
the farthest edge of the sky
the place where the sun rises
the darkest part of the clouds

questions.text: A visitor to the grave may “perplex himself with the purport” of its carving (Ch. XXIV). Here purport means

answers.text: the name of the person buried beneath
the meaning that it carries
the exact date when it was carved
the money it cost to carve

questions.text: Made-up example: The invention of the printing press began a new ______ in Europe.

answers.text: pathos
stigma
epoch
efficacy

questions.text: In “the men of civil eminence” (Ch. XXII), eminence means

answers.text: a large fortune
long experience in office
a loud voice in the council
high rank

questions.text: Which sentence quotes Chapter XIII correctly?

answers.text: Hawthorne writes that she “laid her finger on the scarlet letter” (Ch. XIII).
Hawthorne writes that: she “laid her finger on the scarlet letter” (Ch. XIII).
Hawthorne writes that she “laid her finger on the scarlet letter”. (Ch. XIII)
Hawthorne writes that she “laid her finger on the scarlet letter” Ch. XIII.

questions.text: Hawthorne writes, “The rulers, and the wise and learned men of the community, were longer in acknowledging the influence of Hester’s good qualities than the people” (Ch. XIII). Which version cuts the words after the first comma, up to the next comma, and marks the cut correctly?

answers.text: “The rulers were longer in acknowledging the influence of Hester’s good qualities than the people” (Ch. XIII).
“The rulers ... were longer in acknowledging the influence of Hester’s good qualities than the people” (Ch. XIII).
“The rulers (and the learned men) were longer in acknowledging the influence of Hester’s good qualities than the people” (Ch. XIII).
“The rulers, and the wise and learned men, were longer in acknowledging the influence of Hester’s good qualities than the people” (Ch. XIII).

questions.text: Made-up example: Which sentence grants a point and answers it with the right punctuation?

answers.text: It is true that Hester kept the letter’s meaning from Pearl, however she never once hid the letter itself.
Although Hester kept the letter’s meaning from Pearl, but she never once hid the letter itself.
It is true that Hester kept the letter’s meaning from Pearl; however, she never hid the letter.
While Hester kept the letter’s meaning from Pearl; she never once hid the letter itself.

discussions.title: Should Hester and the Minister Flee?
discussions.html:
Should Hester and the Minister Flee?
English 1 · The Scarlet Letter · Week 3
10 points1 post1 reply
The question
 
In Chapter XVII Hester asks, “Is the world, then, so narrow?” and urges the minister to leave by the forest-track or by sea. At first he answers, “I dare not quit my post” (Ch. XVII). In Chapter XVIII the narrator weighs the choice: “between fleeing as an avowed criminal, and remaining as a hypocrite, conscience might find it hard to strike the balance” (Ch. XVIII). At the end of Chapter XIX the plan still stands, and the scarlet letter is back on Hester’s breast.
Your post (5–7 sentences)
 
1
Take a position: should they flee, should the minister stay and tell the truth, or is neither choice enough?
2
Quote one moment from Chapters XVI–XIX exactly, say who speaks or acts, and cite it like this: (Ch. XVII).
3
Explain how that moment supports your position, and what they owe: the truth, the town, or Pearl.
Your reply (3–4 sentences)
 
Answer a classmate who took a different position or used different evidence. Add a reason, ask a question, or point to a moment they did not use.
